title: The Battle of Manzikert
anachronisms_found: RICHARD_THE_LIONHEART stands in for Emperor Romanos IV Diogenes — an English king of 1189-1199, over a century later and from the wrong culture entirely; the engine offers Byzantine-appropriate alternatives (a generic Cataphract, Emperor Theodore, or an unnamed Knight/Champion renamed) so this was avoidable

GENGHIS_KHAN stands in for Alp Arslan — a Mongol khan of the early 13th century, 150 years after Manzikert and from a different steppe empire; the dialogue even names Alp Arslan, contradicting the placed hero
768 TREE_PALM_FOREST tiles: Manzikert lies on the high, cold Armenian plateau near Lake Van at ~1,700 m; palm forest is desert/tropical vegetation from another region

Seljuk camp built as a CASTLE with 40 STONE_WALL segments and a gate — Alp Arslan's force operated from a mobile field camp, and European donjon-style stone fortification is the wrong architecture for a Seljuk army in the field
PIKEMAN x8 in the Byzantine line — the pike square is a 14th-century development; 11th-century Byzantine infantry were skoutatoi with spears (SPEARMAN would have sufficed, and is also placed)

MAN_AT_ARMS x8 as the Byzantine core with zero heavy cavalry — Romanos' army was built around kataphraktoi and thematic/foreign cavalry, and the engine's Knight/Cataphract line was available (only Player Three has a single KNIGHT)
ROMAN_RUINS as decorative gaia is generic Mediterranean dressing rather than Armenian/Anatolian material culture
strengths: Correct date and place stated in the opening narration (August 1071, the plains near Manzikert), and the two belligerent cultures are at least nominally Byzantine vs Seljuk
The Seljuk player is built almost entirely from CAVALRY_ARCHER, LIGHT_CAVALRY and SCOUT_CAVALRY — a genuinely apt representation of a horse-archer army that fought by harassment and feigned retreat
YURT_A through YURT_D for the Turkic camp is a sensible use of the engine's limited nomadic architecture
The 'Enemy Patrol' and 'Enemy Sortie' PATROL triggers evoke the hit-and-run skirmishing that wore down the Byzantine line before the main engagement
A separate small allied Byzantine contingent (Player Three, with a tent) gestures toward the divided command and the detached wing under Tarchaneiotes/Andronikos Doukas
justification: The scenario names Romanos IV and Alp Arslan in its text but then places Richard the Lionheart and Genghis Khan on the field — two heroes from the wrong centuries and wrong cultures, when AoE2 offered serviceable Byzantine and steppe substitutes. The setting is contradicted by 768 palm-forest trees on what should be the cold Armenian plateau, and the Seljuk field camp is rendered as a stone castle behind 40 wall segments. Most damagingly, the victory logic inverts the history: the player wins by destroying 'Alp Arslan' and keeping Romanos alive, whereas the real battle ended in Byzantine collapse and the emperor's capture (not death, as the [D11] dialogue asserts). The cavalry-archer-heavy Seljuk roster and the patrol/sortie triggers are the one genuinely instructive element.
